newsitem.title: TAIWAN: No fanfare for Chiang's memorial day in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: No fanfare for Chiang's memorial day in Taiwan.

text.p: The media gave it scant coverage and top officials refrained from bombastic eulogies as the memorial day for the death of President Chiang Kai-shek, once a national icon, passed without fanfare in Taiwan on Saturday.

In stark contrast to the pomp of past years, President Lee Teng-hui and other ruling Nationalist Party officials paid respect to the late generalissimo in low-key ceremonies at the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall in Taipei.

Lee and other officials did not make speeches to praise Chiang, who until his death in 1975 ruled Taiwan with an iron hand after his Nationalist forces retreated to the island in 1949 upon losing a Chinese civil war to the communists.

In another sign of Chiang's fading status amid Taiwan's recent political liberalisation, all three state-funded television stations devoted only a few minutes to the coverage of memorial events for Chiang.
The island's two major newspapers -- the United Daily News and the China Times -- made virtually no mention of the national holiday in honour of Chiang.
Chiang's once-indomitable status in Taiwan began to fade when his son, former President Chiang Ching-kuo, launched democratic reforms shortly before his death in 1988.
Taiwan's government, now a full democracy, admitted publicly in February that Chiang kai-shek had ordered the suppression of opposition to Nationalist rule that escalated into a massacre in 1947.
